lesson.objective: Move one cell forward. The robot starts facing up.
hints: The ring is directly ahead of the robot.
One s is one forward move.

lesson.objective: Plan a detour around a wall; blocked moves stay in place.
hints: The direct route is blocked. Look to the right of the wall.
Try three segments: right, up, then left.

lesson.objective: Reuse a side-and-turn procedure four times.
hints: The four sides share one movement pattern.
Put the right turn inside the procedure, after the steps.

lesson.objective: Use one numeric step counter for the long and short sides of a courtyard.
hints: The rectangle is ten cells wide and six cells tall. Broken corner brackets leave both directions open.
Subtract 1 in a recursive walker, then call it with 6 or 10 between turns.

lesson.objective: Pass a diagonal stair unit into a counted repeater, then reuse the complete side.
hints: Each of the four diamond sides contains six diagonal units. Wall brackets and trap beads frame open gaps.
Execute P, then repeat with N-1 and the same P. Wrap one complete side and turn for four uses.

lesson.objective: Grow an instruction parameter by two steps while weaving an open spiral.
hints: The left-turning segments grow 2, 4, 6, up to 18. Wall fragments and trap ribbons echo the turns.
Execute X, turn left and pass Xss onward. The board finishes as soon as all targets are lit.

lesson.objective: Grow a folded out-and-back instruction and rotate three sizes into four petals.
hints: Each folded branch returns to the center with its original heading.
Reuse X six times around the turns, grow X by one step, and rotate the complete three-size motif.

lesson.objective: Compose a counted walk, a fourfold repeater, two lantern frames and their bridge.
hints: The two square frames have six-cell sides and share a straight lower bridge.
Make the frame return to its starting pose, then use the counted walker to cross to its twin.

lesson.objective: Use a finite row count and alternate the connector’s turn direction.
hints: Each row is eight cells long; safe connectors are at the ends.
Adding rr to a turn parameter switches its effective direction.

lesson.objective: Combine counted repetition, shrinking squares and fourfold rotation.
hints: Each quadrant contains squares with sides 6, 4 and 2.
Build one square, recurse with X-2, then rotate the whole motif.

lesson.objective: Combine wall-assisted stops with four returning lantern loops.
hints: Opposite arms have equal lengths; the little loops sit beside their end stops.
A long outward walk can use a wall; count the return distance and preserve the next heading.

lesson.objective: Compose straight rays and diagonal stair rays around a common center.
hints: Four long rays alternate with four shorter diagonal rays. The open gaps connect them.
Give the diagonal step its own counter. Return each ray to the center before rotating.

lesson.objective: Build nested diamonds by reusing a diagonal step and shrinking its count.
hints: The three diamonds have diagonal sides of nine, six and three units.
A diagonal unit preserves heading. Close four sides, then move inward to the next diamond.

lesson.objective: Use separate shrinking and growing recursions to weave a reflected hourglass.
hints: The half-widths shrink 8, 6, 4, 2, then grow 4, 6, 8. Rows are three cells apart.
Return each row to its middle. Treat the narrow waist once when joining the two phases.

lesson.objective: Compose an outward trip, a square lantern and an exact return before rotation.
hints: Each lantern is offset to one side of its spoke; the spaces between spokes stay open.
Make the lantern routine restore its pose. Undo the side turn before walking home.

lesson.objective: Swap two turn arguments while shrinking a folded ribbon, then unwind it.
hints: The four wings use reaches 8, 6, 4, 2 and a fixed two-cell rise.
The child call swaps left and right; after it returns, reverse the two segments of its parent.

lesson.objective: Separate a diagonal walker, one diamond, one row and the complete constellation.
hints: Nine hollow diamonds form a square constellation. Their interiors and the gaps are usable space.
Make one diamond close at its starting pose, then organize the translations separately.

lesson.objective: Use recursive unwinding to return from four nested folds and rotate the shell.
hints: Fold lengths are 11, 8, 5 and 2. Open pockets let you choose how to move between nearby lights.
After visiting the smaller fold, undo its turn and retrace the parent before rotating.

lesson.objective: Visit both recursive branches, restore their parent pose and reflect the whole tree.
hints: Two branching crowns share a center; each has lengths 8, 6, 4 and 2.
Give each child the same return contract. Rotate only after the complete tree returns.

lesson.objective: Exchange rectangle dimensions and turn direction through mutual recursion.
hints: Four sectors overlap at the center. Within a sector, successive loops turn in opposite directions.
Use two procedures with exchanged, reduced dimensions; verify the sector’s heading before reuse.

lesson.objective: Nest a centered window routine inside a two-window sector and a fourfold repeater.
hints: Eight square windows surround a spacious central court; cardinal and corner windows alternate.
Separate the window’s return contract from the sector’s translation and quarter-turn contract.

lesson.objective: Exchange two numeric roles and a turn argument while unfolding four returning vortices.
hints: Horizontal reaches alternate 8, 4, 6, 2; the other dimension advances one cell per two count units.
Keep the two counters distinct. After the child returns, undo the parent using its original arguments.

lesson.objective: Assemble four rotated subcurves by swapping two turn parameters at each level.
hints: The pattern has four similar quarters, each made from four smaller quarters.
Use depth and two opposite turns. The first and fourth subcalls exchange the turns; three two-cell links join them.

lesson.objective: Grow an instruction motif recursively, then execute only the selected expansion level.
hints: Each straight segment becomes five segments with right, left, left, right turns. Four trap caps forbid overrunning the folds.
Carry the expanded instruction as a parameter. A second numeric guard selects the deepest layer before fourfold rotation.

lesson.objective: Place four recursive copies at offsets, using depth and spacing as independent parameters.
hints: Four large corner groups contain four smaller groups; each connector must be retraced.
Factor a corner trip that returns rotated by a quarter turn; repeat it four times and reduce spacing by three in each child.

lesson.objective: Use two mutually recursive turns to generate a folding curve rather than a repeated tile.
hints: The two halves have related folds, but their turns are ordered differently.
One procedure expands A, right, B, walk, right; its partner expands left, walk, A, left, B.

lesson.objective: Construct inverse recursive procedures so a folded curve returns before its next rotation.
hints: Four folded arms share a center. Finishing a curve does not automatically restore its starting pose.
Reverse the order of each recursive body and exchange left with right; surround the inverse trip with half turns.

lesson.objective: Combine a branching return invariant with chirality passed through four recursive levels.
hints: The same branch is reflected differently in its two children, then reused in four directions.
Pass depth, stem length and a turn. Reverse the turn for one child; return to the parent pose after both children.

lesson.objective: Nest window, row, shrinking tier and rotation routines, each with its own return invariant.
hints: Each sector has three tiers: three large windows, two medium windows, one small window.
Let the row recurse sideways and unwind back; let the tier recurse upward and unwind down, then rotate the whole sector.

lesson.objective: Compose a window generator with a chiral branching tree and a higher-order rotation routine.
hints: Every node is both a square courtyard and a branch junction; depth, size and chirality change independently.
Prove the courtyard and each subtree return to the same pose. Build one sector from those contracts, then pass it to a fourfold repeater.

lesson.objective: Weave a closed space-filling loop across four quadrants by linking rotated Hilbert quarters.
hints: Unlike the open Hilbert curve where start and end lie in opposite corners, the Moore curve forms an unbroken closed loop with 4-fold rotational symmetry returning to its origin.
Factor a recursive Hilbert subcurve with turn-swapping, then embed it into a fourfold repeater with connector links.

lesson.objective: Traverse two interlocking fractal dragon arms with 180-degree point symmetry.
hints: The board exhibits pure 2-fold central inversion symmetry: every feature in the northern quadrant has an identical counterpart rotated 180 degrees into the southern quadrant.
Build an asymmetric tree arm with dynamic turn inversion rrT, then pass it as an embedded argument to a two-fold inverter procedure.

lesson.objective: Generate a bilateral fractal canopy with pure vertical mirror symmetry across the central axis.
hints: The pattern possesses exact bilateral reflection symmetry: the left wing is a mirror reflection of the right wing across the vertical line x=12.
Define a recursive branching arm, then pass mirrored calls with opposing chiral turns into a higher-order dual dispatcher.

lesson.objective: Traverse a space-filling serpentine meander spanning four symmetric quadrants.
hints: The nested serpentine meander divides space recursively, preserving 4-fold rotational symmetry around the center.
Compose serpentine folds with inward parameter decay, and drive it through an embedded call inside a fourfold repeater.

lesson.objective: Synthesize an 8-fold dihedral fractal snowflake star with multi-level triangular promontories.
hints: The snowflake exhibits full 8-fold dihedral symmetry (D4), combining 4-fold rotation with diagonal and axial reflections.
Branch each arm recursively into dual sub-arms with opposite chiral turns, then wrap in an embedded fourfold dispatcher.

lesson.objective: Master asymmetric tree recursion: traverse unbalanced N-1 and N-2 subtrees and restore caller pose.
hints: A Fibonacci tree branches with different decay rates: the left branch recurses with N-1 while the right recurses with N-2.
The return path cannot mirror a uniform child. Explicitly retrace distance D after both subtrees finish, wrapped in an embedded call.

lesson.objective: Interleave two independent clock frequencies to weave a poly-periodic harmonic lattice.
hints: Two counters decrementing at different rates trigger staggered termination conditions while preserving exact return invariants.
Maintain dual parameters A and B with chiral turn inversion, retrace along the conjugate path, and embed in a fourfold repeater.

lesson.objective: Execute a binary reflected Gray code sequence, recursing through inner chambers before each pivot step.
hints: The classic Tower of Hanoi sequence visits states without redundant passes: G(N) expands into G(N-1), step, G(N-1).
Procedure g(N, T) calls g(N-1, rrT), advances b(N), executes turn T, calls g(N-1, T), and unwinds b(N), embedded in a dispatcher.

lesson.objective: Harmonize cardinal steps and diagonal staircase walkers across three concentric octagonal tiers with 8-fold dihedral symmetry.
hints: Four cardinal spokes and four diagonal stair rays radiate simultaneously, creating an 8-fold dihedral (D4) star polygon.
Pair cardinal walk b(S) with diagonal stair d(N), retrace each symmetrically, and invoke via mutually recursive embedded dispatcher a(N,S):q(m(N,S)r).

lesson.objective: Synthesize concentric courtyards, asymmetric Fibonacci spires, and orbital rotations into a grandmaster capstone.
hints: Four quadrants each contain a courtyard chamber and an unbalanced asymmetric recursive spire branching into deep space.
Compose courtyard generator c(W), Fibonacci tree f(N, D, T), and sector orchestrator a(N, D, T), driven by an embedded call inside repeater q.

lesson.objective: Swap shrinking rectangle dimensions and chirality while restoring every entrance pose.
hints: Each quadrant contains three offset rectangles. Their long side changes direction at the next level.
Separate the closed rectangle from its two-part connector. Swap width, height and turns only in the child, then undo the connector.

lesson.objective: Grow a forward instruction and its inverse together, then execute one selected expansion.
hints: Four folded arms end in square loops. The return must undo the folds in reverse order.
Carry two instruction parameters. If the next forward path is X-right-Y, its inverse is X-left-Y; use a separate numeric guard to execute the final pair.

lesson.objective: Coordinate shrinking widths, growing heights and row offsets with separate return invariants.
hints: Each row has three windows. Moving right reduces width and increases height; the next row starts narrower and taller.
Make a rectangle return to its corner, a row return along its changing spacings, and the outer recursion restore each seven-cell rise.

lesson.objective: Alternate branch sides as reach shrinks and the terminal window grows, then unwind the central spine.
hints: Along an arm, side reaches are five, four and three cells while window sides are one, two and three.
Keep depth, reach and window size independent. Finish each side trip before advancing the spine; invert the turn only for the child.

lesson.objective: Replace each recursive curve link with a reusable window-and-walk instruction without changing its pose contract.
hints: Small square windows follow a larger folded curve. The connector has the same net displacement as a three-cell walk.
Pass the window-and-walk as an instruction argument to the curve. Its closed window must restore heading before the three-cell link.

lesson.objective: Build inverse stair walkers and reuse them through unequal, mirrored recursive branches.
hints: Branches move diagonally with stair steps. Repeating the forward stair after a half turn does not retrace it.
Reverse the stair unit and exchange its turns. Give each subtree a returning pose contract before combining depths N-1 and N-2.

lesson.objective: Place unequal recursive courtyards at alternating corners, with swapped dimensions and chirality.
hints: A large rectangular circuit holds a child at each corner. Adjacent children shrink different dimensions.
Factor a two-corner half circuit and repeat it twice. Each child must close at its own corner before the parent continues.

lesson.objective: Nest returning windows inside shrinking rows while window size grows between tiers.
hints: The tiers have three, two and one windows. Within a row they shrink; between rows the first window grows.
Give inner nesting, sideways translation and upward translation separate recursions; all three must undo their displacement.

lesson.objective: Dock with four decorated recursive curves and construct the inverse of both the curve and its link motif.
hints: Each quadrant has a folded panel. A square at the far end must be visited before retracing to the shared center.
Invert a decorated link by walking first and drawing the mirrored square afterward. Use reversed turn arguments for the return curve.

lesson.objective: Combine inverse diagonal trunks, unequal subtrees and exchanged node motifs into one returning recursive system.
hints: Square and diamond nodes share diagonal branches. One child exchanges the two motifs and the turns; its sibling retains them.
Make both node instructions close at their entry pose. Pass them alongside depth, stride and turns, and retrace each stair trunk after both children.
